mainTopic: An אונן on ערב פסח and the קרבן פסח: רב מרי's day-of-death answer fails, and אביי's before/after midday split is proven from two ברייתות.
overview: רבי שמעון seems to contradict himself about an אונן on ערב פסח. In one place, he may not take part in the קרבן פסח. In another, he cites the rule that 'an אונן immerses and eats his קרבן פסח at night.' רב מרי answers that the first case is a death on the 14th, which is Torah-level mourning. The second is a burial on the 14th after a death on the 13th, which is only rabbinic. רב אשי shows this would make רבי שמעון's proof to רבי יהודה pointless, and the גמרא leaves רב מרי with a difficulty. אביי answers instead that it depends on whether the death was before or after midday on the 14th, since from midday the person is already fit for the קרבן פסח. The גמרא supports this from two ברייתות that seem to clash. In one, יוסף הכהן was forced to become impure for his wife on ערב פסח. In the other, a person on his way to his פסח may not become impure for a relative. The גמרא considers that the clash is just a מחלוקת between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא. It then shows that both ברייתות are רבי עקיבא's, so the before/after midday split stands.

steps.title: רב מרי's answer: day of death versus day of burial
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי resolves the contradiction in רבי שמעון by saying each statement deals with a different case: death and burial both on the 14th, or death on the 13th and burial on the 14th.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is no contradiction. One statement is where the relative died on the 14th of ניסן and was buried on the 14th. The other is where he died on the 13th and was buried on the 14th.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction between רבי שמעון's two statements by giving each one its own case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'no קרבן פסח' statement is about a relative who died on the 14th itself. The 'immerses and eats his קרבן פסח' rule is about a relative who died on the 13th and was only buried on the 14th. The next step explains why that difference matters.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
Here... here; this case... that case
A close relative of his died
He buried him

phrases.english: It is not difficult;

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן שֶׁמֵּת לוֹ מֵת בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר
phrases.english: here, it is where his relative died on the fourteenth
phrases.notes: The fourteenth of ניסן, the day the קרבן פסח is brought. This is the case where he may not bring it.

phrases.english: and he buried him on the fourteenth;

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן שֶׁמֵּת לוֹ מֵת בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר
phrases.english: there, it is where his relative died on the thirteenth
phrases.notes: This is the case where the rule 'an אונן immerses and eats his פסח' applies.

phrases.english: and he buried him on the fourteenth.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא; כָּאן שֶׁמֵּת לוֹ מֵת בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction between רבי שמעון's two statements, which was raised just before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source is about a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements seem to be about the same אונן on ערב פסח, so they seem to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: One is about the day of death; the other is about a burial day that came after an earlier death.

steps.title: Why the day matters: Torah-level versus rabbinic mourning
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי explains his split. אנינות on the day of death is from the Torah and carries over into the night. אנינות on a burial day is only rabbinic, so its night is only rabbinic too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he died on the 14th and was buried on the 14th, the day of death carries over into its night by Torah law. If he died on the 13th and was buried on the 14th, the burial day is only rabbinic, and it carries over into its night only by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind the split from step 1. It is all about how strong the mourning is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אנינות on the day of death is דאורייתא, and it 'grabs' the following night at the Torah level, so the קרבן פסח cannot push it aside. A burial day is only אנינות דרבנן, and its night is only rabbinic. The Torah מצוה of eating the קרבן פסח overrides that, so he immerses and eats.

keyTerms.meaning: The day of death
The day of burial
Takes hold of its night; the mourning carries over into the following night
By Torah law
By rabbinic law

steps.confusionAlert: The night here is the night of the 15th, when the קרבן פסח is eaten. The question is whether the mourning from the day before still applies at that time, and at what level.

phrases.english: If his relative died on the fourteenth
and he buried him on the fourteenth,
the day of death takes hold of its night by Torah law.
If his relative died on the thirteenth
and he buried him on the fourteenth,
the day of burial is only by rabbinic law,
so it takes hold of its night only by rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת לוֹ מֵת בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר וּקְבָרוֹ בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the case split in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the logic of the split: the mourning is דאורייתא in one case and דרבנן in the other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Torah-level אנינות on the night blocks the קרבן פסח. Rabbinic-level אנינות on the night does not.

steps.title: רב אשי: רבי שמעון's proof would then make no sense
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges רב מרי. רבי שמעון cited the rule 'an אונן immerses and eats his פסח' as a proof against רבי יהודה. If that rule is only about a rabbinic burial day, רבי יהודה could simply wave the proof away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רב מרי: Then what about the ברייתא where רבי שמעון said, 'Know that this is so, for they said: an אונן immerses and eats his קרבן פסח, but not other קדשים'? רבי יהודה could answer him: 'I am talking about the day of death, which is Torah law, and you are bringing me a proof about the day of burial, which is only rabbinic?!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks רב מרי's answer. He shows it would turn רבי שמעון's own proof into a pointless argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי שמעון brought this rule to prove his position to רבי יהודה. If the rule only covers a burial day, which is דרבנן, it says nothing about a Torah-level day of death. רבי יהודה could easily reject the proof. A תנא would not bring such a weak proof, so רב מרי's reading of the rule seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: But then, if so... (opens a challenge)
Know that this is so (introduces a proof)
A mourner on the day a close relative dies, before burial
Immerses in a מקוה
Other sacrificial meat
Let him say to him; he could have answered

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב מָרִי:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Rav Mari:
But then, what about that which is taught:
Rabbi Shimon said to him: Know that this is so,
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי יהודה, the one רבי שמעון is arguing with in that ברייתא.

phrases.english: for they said:
An acute mourner immerses and eats his Paschal offering
but not other sacrificial meat.
Let him answer him:
phrases.notes: With רב מרי's reading, רבי יהודה could easily reply to רבי שמעון like this.

phrases.aramaic: קָאָמֵינָא לָךְ אֲנָא יוֹם מִיתָה דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא,
phrases.english: I am telling you about the day of death, which is Torah law,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרַתְּ לִי אֶת יוֹם קְבוּרָה דְּרַבָּנַן?!
phrases.english: and you tell me about the day of burial, which is rabbinic?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב מָרִי: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב מרי's answer from steps 1 and 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מרי's claim that the rule 'an אונן eats his פסח' is about a burial day, which is only דרבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון used that rule as a proof about Torah-level אנינות. If it were only about rabbinic mourning, the proof would fail and רבי יהודה could easily reject it.

steps.title: The challenge stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that רב אשי's challenge is a real difficulty for רב מרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that רב מרי's answer has no defense against רב אשי's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The single word 'קשיא' means the question stays unanswered. It is not a full rejection of רב מרי, but it opens the door for a different answer, which comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a difficulty; the challenge remains unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: רב מרי's split (day of death versus burial day) is left with an unanswered challenge, because it would make רבי שמעון's proof to רבי יהודה pointless.

phrases.english: It is a difficulty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of step 3 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב מרי's resolution stays under a difficulty, so the גמרא looks for another answer.

steps.title: אביי's answer: before midday versus after midday
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a new way to resolve the contradiction in רבי שמעון. It depends on whether the relative died before or after midday on the 14th of ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is not difficult. Here, it is where he died before midday. There, it is where he died after midday.
steps.whatsHappening: After רב מרי's answer ran into trouble, אביי offers a different way to split the two statements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the death is on the 14th itself, so this answer avoids רב אשי's problem. The only difference is the time of death. Before midday, he may not bring the קרבן פסח. After midday, he immerses and eats it that night.

keyTerms.meaning: Before midday
After midday

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult;
here, it is where he died before midday,
phrases.notes: Midday of the fourteenth of ניסן.

phrases.english: there, it is where he died after midday.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: לָא קַשְׁיָא; כָּאן שֶׁמֵּת קוֹדֶם חֲצוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new answer, replacing רב מרי's, which was left with a difficulty.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different case split, based on the time of death during the 14th.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: After רב מרי failed, the contradiction in רבי שמעון seems to be back.
steps.terutzMaskana: Death before midday blocks the קרבן פסח. Death after midday does not.

steps.title: Why midday matters: was he already fit for the פסח?
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains his split. Before midday the person was not yet fit for the קרבן פסח, so אנינות takes hold of him. After midday he was already fit for it, so אנינות does not take hold with regard to the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Before midday, when he was not yet fit for the פסח, אנינות takes hold of him. After midday, when he was already fit for the פסח, אנינות does not take hold of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind אביי's midday split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The time for the קרבן פסח begins at midday on the 14th. If the death came first, the mourning took hold before the פסח obligation began, so he cannot bring it. If the obligation was already in place when the death happened, the mourning cannot take hold of him with regard to the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Was fit for or eligible for
Takes effect on him
The status of an אונן; acute mourning

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, what decides the case is which came first: the death or midday on the 14th, when the person becomes fit for the קרבן פסח.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea: once a person is already fit for the קרבן פסח, a status that comes later (here, אנינות) does not take hold of him with regard to it.

phrases.english: Before midday, when he was not yet fit for the Paschal offering,
acute mourning takes effect on him.
After midday, when he was already fit for the Paschal offering,
acute mourning does not take effect on him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for אביי's split in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the logic: being fit for the פסח first stops אנינות from taking hold.
steps.terutzMaskana: If he was fit for the פסח before the death, אנינות does not block him from eating it.

steps.title: Where do we see a before-midday and after-midday split?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that the law really changes depending on whether the death was before or after midday.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where do we see that it makes a difference whether it happened before midday or after midday?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for אביי's split. This is a setup question, and the next steps bring the sources that answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי gave a logical reason for his split in Step 6. Now the גמרא wants to show the split already exists in earlier sources, so it is not just a new idea.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this? (asking for a source)
Midday. On the 14th of ניסן, this is when the time for the קרבן פסח begins.
It is different. There is a difference.

phrases.english: And from where do you say
that there is a difference for him

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין קוֹדֶם חֲצוֹת בֵּין לְאַחַר חֲצוֹת?
phrases.english: between before midday and after midday?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source backing אביי's before/after midday split.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the time of death, before or after midday, changes the law.

steps.title: A כהן is forced to become impure for his wife on ערב פסח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a כהן must become impure for a close relative, even against his will. In a story, יוסף הכהן's wife died on ערב פסח, and the כהנים made him impure against his will.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: "For her may he become impure." This is a מצוה. If he does not want to, they make him impure against his will. There was a story with יוסף הכהן, whose wife died on ערב פסח. He did not want to become impure, but his fellow כהנים voted and made him impure against his will.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the first source. It shows that on ערב פסח, a כהן still had to become impure for his dead wife, even though that meant missing the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא shows that his obligation to his dead relative was stronger than his wish to bring the פסח. By itself it seems to say that a death on ערב פסח always pushes away the פסח. The next source will seem to say the opposite.

keyTerms.meaning: For her may he become impure. The פסוק about a כהן and his close relatives.
Against his will
And they voted. They took a count and decided.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
"For her may he become impure": it is a מצוה.
If he did not want to,
they make him impure against his will.
And there was an incident with יוסף the כהן
whose wife died on the eve of פסח,
and he did not want to become impure,
and his brothers the כהנים voted
and made him impure against his will.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the first source in answer to the question.
steps.raayaObject: That a death on ערב פסח can obligate a person in his relative's burial, even though it costs him the פסח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on ויקרא 21:3 together with the story of יוסף הכהן.

steps.title: A contradicting ברייתא: on the way to his פסח, he may not become impure
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא learns from "ולאחותו" that a person on his way to slaughter his פסח or circumcise his son may not become impure when he hears that a relative died.
steps.simpleTranslation: They contrasted it with another ברייתא: Why does the פסוק say "or for his sister"? Take someone who went to slaughter his פסח or to circumcise his son, and he heard that a relative of his died. You might think he should become impure. The answer is: he shall not become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that seems to say the opposite of the first one. Here, a death on ערב פסח does not allow him to become impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first ברייתא, becoming impure for a relative on ערב פסח was required. In this ברייתא, it is forbidden. This clash is what will prove אביי's split.

keyTerms.meaning: And they set it against another source. This brings a contradiction.
Why does the פסוק need to say this?
You might have thought
You said. This introduces the answer that comes from the פסוק.

phrases.english: And they contrasted it with another source:
"Or for his sister": why does the verse need to say it?
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:7. This פסוק is talking about a נזיר.

phrases.english: Here is one who went to slaughter his פסח
or to circumcise his son,
and he heard that a relative of his died.
You might think he should become impure?
You said: he shall not become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a second ברייתא against the first one to create a contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא of יוסף הכהן, where becoming impure on ערב פסח was required.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here a person facing the פסח may not become impure for a relative, which is the opposite of the first ברייתא.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: a מת מצוה is different
steps.stepSummary: The second ברייתא adds that the word "ולאחותו" limits the rule. He may not become impure for his sister, but he must become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that just as he may not become impure for his sister, he also may not become impure for a מת מצוה. That is why the פסוק says "or for his sister": for his sister he does not become impure, but for a מת מצוה he does become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The second ברייתא keeps going. It explains that the ban applies only to a relative, and not to a dead person with no one else to bury him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This finishes the ברייתא's reading of "ולאחותו". The word teaches two things: he does not become impure for a relative at this time, but he does become impure for a מת מצוה. The main point for our סוגיא is still the first half, that he may not become impure for a relative while facing the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: A dead person with no one else to bury him. Anyone who finds him must bury him.
Just as... so too

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this part is the contradiction. The contradiction with יוסף הכהן comes from the relative case in Step 9. The מת מצוה part just completes the ברייתא.

phrases.english: You might think that just as he may not become impure for his sister,
so too he may not become impure for a מת מצוה?
The verse says: "or for his sister."
It is for his sister that he does not become impure,
but he does become impure for a מת מצוה.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even while facing the פסח, a person must become impure to bury a מת מצוה, though not for his relative.

steps.title: The answer: one case is before midday, the other after
steps.stepSummary: The only way to settle the two ברייתות is that יוסף הכהן's case was before midday and the second case was after midday. This proves אביי's split.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't we learn from this: here it was before midday, and there it was after midday?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests settling the contradiction with אביי's split, which would prove that the time of death, before or after midday, really matters. The next step questions this proof, and Steps 13–15 restore it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before midday, the duty of the פסח had not yet started, so the duty to the dead relative took hold first. That is why יוסף הכהן was made impure. After midday, he was already obligated in the פסח, so he may not become impure for a relative.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't we learn from this? This introduces a proof.

steps.whatToRemember: The two ברייתות are not arguing. יוסף הכהן's wife died before midday, so he had to become impure. In the second ברייתא, the death came after midday, when he was already obligated in the פסח, so he may not become impure. This backs up אביי.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that אביי's before/after midday split is not new. It is built into earlier sources, and that makes it a strong answer to the contradiction in רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: Don't we learn from this:
here it is before midday,
phrases.notes: "Here" is יוסף הכהן's case. "There" is the case of the one on his way to slaughter his פסח.

phrases.english: and there it is after midday?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: כָּאן קוֹדֶם חֲצוֹת, כָּאן לְאַחַר חֲצוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the contradiction between Steps 8 and 9, which proves אביי's split.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's split: a death before midday on the 14th obligates the person toward the dead, but a death after midday does not override the פסח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The only way to settle the ברייתא of יוסף הכהן with the ברייתא on "ולאחותו".

steps.title: Maybe the two ברייתות are an argument between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests both ברייתות are after midday. One follows רבי ישמעאל, who says impurity for a relative is optional, and the other follows רבי עקיבא, who says it is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know that is the answer? Maybe both cases are after midday. One ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל and the other follows רבי עקיבא. A ברייתא teaches: 'For her he may become impure.' That is optional, says רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says it is required.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof from Step 11. It offers a different way to explain why the two ברייתות disagree, one that has nothing to do with midday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל holds that a כהן is never required to become impure for a relative, so he can easily say a person on his way to his פסח should stay pure. רבי עקיבא holds it is a חובה, which fits the story where יוסף הכהן was made impure against his will. If this is true, the two ברייתות are simply a מחלוקת, and nothing proves אביי's split.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know? It questions a conclusion.
This one and that one, meaning both cases
Optional, allowed but not required
Required, an obligation

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a final ruling. The גמרא is testing whether the proof for אביי's split really holds, and it will reject this suggestion in the next step.

phrases.english: From where do you know this?
Perhaps, actually, I will say to you:
both this case and that case are after midday;

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְהָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.english: and this one follows Rabbi Yishmael, and that one follows Rabbi Akiva.
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא about not becoming impure follows רבי ישמעאל, and the story of יוסף הכהן follows רבי עקיבא.

steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The contradiction could come from a מחלוקת between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא, not from the time of day.

steps.title: The ברייתא about the נזיר is רבי עקיבא's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. The opening of the ברייתא about the נזיר is taught in רבי עקיבא's name, explaining 'נפש' as relatives and 'מת' as non-relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not think that. The first part of that ברייתא is taught by רבי עקיבא. A ברייתא says that רבי עקיבא explains: 'נפש' refers to relatives, and 'מת' refers to non-relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the suggestion in Step 12. It shows that the ברייתא about not becoming impure is actually רבי עקיבא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא about the נזיר follows רבי עקיבא, then it cannot be רבי ישמעאל's view. Both ברייתות now follow the same תנא, so the contradiction between them comes back.

steps.title: Father, mother, brother: even a very holy person buries a מת מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא's ברייתא goes through the words 'לאביו', 'לאמו', and 'לאחיו'. Each one teaches that a נזיר does not become impure for that relative, even when he is also a כהן or a כהן גדול, but he does become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For his father' he does not become impure, but he does for a מת מצוה. 'For his mother': if he was a כהן and also a נזיר, he does not become impure for his mother, but he does for a מת מצוה. 'For his brother': if he was a כהן גדול and also a נזיר, he does not become impure for his brother, but he does for a מת מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting רבי עקיבא's full ברייתא. Each relative named in the פסוק teaches a new lesson about the מת מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word adds a stronger case. A plain נזיר, then a כהן who is also a נזיר, then a כהן גדול who is also a נזיר. Even with all these extra layers of holiness, he still must bury a מת מצוה. The point for the סוגיא is that all of this is still רבי עקיבא speaking.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר, even one who is also a כהן or a כהן גדול, does not become impure for his father, mother, or brother, but he must become impure for a מת מצוה.

steps.title: The 'ולאחותו' teaching is also רבי עקיבא's
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with the 'ולאחותו' lesson about one going to his פסח or his son's ברית. This is the same teaching quoted earlier, and it is part of רבי עקיבא's ברייתא. So both ברייתות follow רבי עקיבא, and אביי's midday split stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the פסוק say 'and for his sister'? Take a person who went to slaughter his פסח or circumcise his son, and he heard that a relative died. Might he become impure? You say: he may not. Might he also not become impure for a מת מצוה, just as for his sister? The פסוק says 'and for his sister': for his sister he may not become impure, but he does become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי עקיבא's ברייתא. Its last part is the very teaching that seemed to clash with the story of יוסף הכהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'ולאחותו' teaching sits inside רבי עקיבא's own ברייתא. So the idea that it follows רבי ישמעאל falls apart. With both ברייתות following רבי עקיבא, the only way to settle them is the before/after midday split, so the proof for אביי returns.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the פסוק come to teach?
One might have thought

steps.whatToRemember: Both ברייתות follow רבי עקיבא, who holds that a כהן must become impure for a relative. The clash between them can only be settled by time: before midday he becomes impure, after midday he does not. That is אביי's split.
steps.confusionAlert: This text was already quoted in Steps 9 and 10. It is repeated here for a new reason: to show that it belongs to רבי עקיבא's ברייתא.

phrases.english: "And for his sister": what does the verse come to teach?
Here is one who went to slaughter his Paschal offering
or to circumcise his son,
and he heard that a relative of his died,
one might think he should become impure?
You say: he may not become impure.
One might think that just as he does not become impure for his sister,
so too he does not become impure for a met מצוה?
The verse teaches: "And for his sister":
for his sister he may not become impure,
but he does become impure for a met מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי עקיבא's ברייתא and shows that the 'ולאחותו' teaching from Steps 9 and 10 is part of it.
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא about not becoming impure on the way to the פסח follows רבי עקיבא, which brings back the proof for אביי's split.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The full ברייתא of רבי עקיבא, which includes the 'ולאחותו' teaching.
steps.whyThisMatters: It removes the 'two תנאים' escape route, so the proof from Step 11 for אביי's before/after midday split stands.
